*
* Title: saclevel
* Author: Kerry Clark
* Date Written: 03/07/94
* Oracle Vers. Orig.: 7.0
* Forms Vers. Orig.: 3.0
* Revision History:
*
* Modified By Date Ver Description
* ---------------------------------------------------------------
* Kerry Clark 03/07/94 0.0 Initial Version
* Michael Hoang 06/03/94 1.0 updated for database changes
* Michael Hoang 06/08/94 1.1 screen design changes, fixed bugs
* Michael Hoang 06/16/94 1.1 fixed customer_id
* Mark Hansen 08/26/94 1.2 fixed AR's in Struct. Testing
* Kerry Clark 10/12/94 1.3 fixed AR's in Struct. Testing
* Kerry Clark 11/03/94 1.4 structural testing sm250,301,
* 303,304
* duplicate record problems, see
* test_for_dup_att, eff_date problems
* allows change only if new record
* and allows you to tab through the
* existing field if no eff date changed
*
* Abstract:
* This form will allow the user to input optimum and minimum
* inventory levels based on product code, blood type,
* effective date and termination date. This form is used
* to build a validation table for blood centers only.
*
* Menu Reference:
* Check_Package_Failure, Handle_Error, Nullchk, Show_Error,
*
* Error Conditions:
*
* show_error('0319'); -- duplicate entry not allowed
* show_error('0000'); -- transaction committed
* show_error('1180'); -- invalid function key
* show_error('5320'); -- Invalid chapter ID
* show_error('0230'); -- uncessful commit.. transaction not committed
* show_error('5307'); -- invalid inventory class
* show_error('5302'); -- invalid inventory type
* show_error('0309'); -- invalid product code
* show_error('0300'); -- invalid blood type
* show_error('5310'); -- Invalid Inventory code.
* show_error('5304'); -- Invalid Product Code Entered.
* show_error('5308'); -- Invalid quantity,must be zero or greater.
*
* Inputs:
* Chapter ID
* Inventory Class
* Product Code
* Blood Type
* Effective Date
* Termination Date
* Minimal and optimal inventory levels.
*
* Outputs:
* Update the following tables:
* 1) set_inventory_levels
*
* Modules Referenced:
* Check_Package_Failure, Handle_Error, Nullchk, Show_Error,
*
* Assumptions and Limitations:
* None.
*
* Functional Descriptions:
* This form will take inputs from the user and insert/update
* set inventory levels. It will allow you to update the inventory
* quantity for each level defined.
*
***************************************************************************

ProgramUnit.Name: TEST_FOR_DUP_ATTR
ProgramUnit.ProgramUnitText:
procedure test_for_dup_attr (dup out VARCHAR2) is
--
-- Test_for_dup_field is a general purpose utility that checks all
-- non-query records (those that have not been committed) for duplicates
-- that may exist on screen for a specific field in a base table.
--
-- Input variable 'field' is ascii field name for the base block (table)
-- and does not need the table name prepended.
--
-- Input/Output variable 'dup' returns TRUE if there is a record with a
-- duplicate field somewhere else on the screen, but has not been
-- committed to the database.
--
-- NOTE: this procedure will leave the cursor in the same field and
-- record that it was in prior to entry. It is up to the trigger that
-- called this procedure to position the cursor elsewhere. Also, this
-- procedure does not search any tables or database, only non-committed
-- records in the form.
--
 original_field VARCHAR2(50); -- 50 may be too large, but it seems
 original_rec VARCHAR2(5);
 orig_inv_type VARCHAR2(2);
 orig_prd_type VARCHAR2(5);
 orig_abo_type VARCHAR2(4);
 orig_att_grp VARCHAR2(10);
 orig_att_code VARCHAR2(4);
begin
 original_field := :system.cursor_field;
 original_rec := :system.trigger_record; -- save the record #
 orig_inv_type := :levels.inventory_type;
 orig_prd_type := :levels.product_type;
 orig_abo_type := :levels.blood_type;
 orig_att_grp := :attrib_group;
 orig_att_code := :attrib_code;
 go_record('1'); -- start with the top
 dup := '0'; -- assume no duplicates
 loop
 if orig_inv_type = :levels.inventory_type
 and orig_prd_type = :levels.product_type
 and orig_abo_type = :levels.blood_type
 -- and orig_att_grp = :attrib_group
 -- and orig_att_code = :attrib_code
 and :system.trigger_record != original_rec
 then
 dup := '1';
 exit;
 end if;
 if :system.last_record = 'FALSE' -- if not last record,
 then -- ..position downward
 down;
 else
 exit;
 end if;
 end loop;
 go_record(original_rec); -- restore cursor
 GO_ITEM(original_field); -- ..position
end;
